A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Faire research. The main text, equations, Tables 1–7, Figures 1–17, and Appendices A–F are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original Faire evaluations, training and reward ablations, entropy analysis, and human-rating comparisons in Section 5, plus GGBench results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices, including the ablations and GGBench evaluation.

M1.justification: The GeoGebra interleaved reasoning procedure, geometric/perceptual/semantic verifiers, SFT initialization, and GRPO reward and optimization formulation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Faire-Bench plane geometry, analytic geometry, and function tasks, together with GenExam and GGBench evaluations. No training domain or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main comparison, GenExam evaluation, and GGBench evaluation (Tables 2, 3, and 7). The switch to numbered citations does not introduce different baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain the 4,643/2,321/1,025 SFT/RL/evaluation split, Qwen3-VL-8B initialization, two SFT epochs, and seven GRPO candidates per prompt at temperature 0.9. Appendix A's evaluation metrics and procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The reward and training-paradigm ablations, token-entropy analysis, human-rating comparison, category-wise analysis, and geometry case studies are retained. Relocating their displays adds no new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed-based variability, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain the same human-rating correlation, r = 0.9578, with unchanged statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. Examples include Faire's 74.82 accuracy and 45.37 verification average in Table 2, 52.3 Math-Rel and 9.3 Math-Str in Table 3, and 63.13 overall GGBench score in Table 7.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 retain the same trajectory definitions, entropy arguments, verification constraints, reward and GRPO objective, and evaluation definitions. No mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same SFT-paradox claim, functional-alignment explanation, Faire contribution, and claimed benchmark advantages. Their scientific scope and strength are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of SFT failure, RL-induced functional grounding, entropy shifts, human agreement, and GGBench performance are retained. Appendix A's qualifications about surface-similarity metrics also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendices A and C retain the same training settings, hardware/software disclosures, processing rules, and three verifier prompts. No implementation detail or code/data access information is substantively added or removed.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to geometry solvers, interleaved generation methods, and existing benchmarks remain the same. Bibliography reordering and conversion from author-year to numbered citations are presentation changes.

P1.justification: v2 revises affiliations and front matter, changes Section 5 from 'Experiment' to 'Experimental', adds an Appendix heading, removes the generic Impact Statement, and restyles citations and references. Scientific prose and the section sequence are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column, ByteDance-branded design with a boxed abstract and blue headings. Figures and tables are extensively resized or relocated, and captions and appendix prompt boxes are restyled. Their scientific content is retained.

improvement.justification: The method, arguments, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information are unchanged. The redesign enlarges some main-text graphics but separates appendix prompts and GGBench displays further from their discussion. These presentation tradeoffs, minor editorial edits, and removal of generic impact discussion leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
